name: Madurese
notes: Madurese (Bhâsa Madhurâ) in the Latin orthography (Alfabet Latèn); a Javanese-script orthography also exists and is not covered here. Distinctive three-way laryngeal contrast in stops — voiceless unaspirated, voiced, and a breathy/aspirated series written with ⟨h⟩ digraphs (bh, dh, jh, gh). Nine vowels; the Latin norm writes /ɛ/ as ⟨è⟩ and /ɤ/ as ⟨â⟩, while plain ⟨e⟩ covers /ə/ and /ɨ/, so ⟨e⟩ is genuinely ambiguous. Retroflex ṭ/ḍ and the retroflex nasal are dialectal/typographic variants not represented in the base map.

sources.notes: Orthography note (p. 109) and the consonant table with one spelled word per phoneme (p. 110), read in full; the spelling used is the 2008 Balai Bahasa Surabaya system. It corroborates ⟨â⟩ = ɤ, ⟨è⟩ = ɛ, ⟨e⟩ = ə, ⟨ny ng⟩ = ɲ ŋ and the plain voiced series ⟨b d g⟩. It contradicts this map on the ⟨h⟩ digraphs: ⟨bh dh jh gh⟩ are the voiceless aspirated pʰ tʰ cʰ kʰ (bhârâng /pʰɤɾɤŋ/, dhâlem /tʰɤlɘm/, jhâlâ /cʰɤlɤ/, ghâghâ /kʰɤkʰɤ/), not the breathy-voiced bʱ dʱ dʒʱ ɡʱ the map emits; ⟨c j⟩ are the palatal stops c ɟ, not tʃ dʒ; and the retroflex series ⟨ṭ ṭh ḍ⟩ (written with a dot in the 2008 system) has no key in the map at all. Recorded here; the grapheme data is not changed in this citation.

ancestors.notes: Malayo-Polynesian, the Austronesian branch containing every Austronesian language outside Formosa.
